services.desc: Can’t make it to Montana? The National Museum of Forest Service History presents these virtual exhibits for anyone to discover and enjoy. By Charlie Richmond and John Steffenson, National Museum of Forest Service History Case No. 1 was the name given to an 1899 timber sale on U.S. Government land in the Black Hills Forest Reserve in South Dakota. Under this contract, 13 million board feet of ponderosa pine trees were cut from the Forest Reserve by the Homestake Mining Company. Jim Girard worked with trees his whole life - from his youth making whiskey barrels in the hills of Tennessee, to his esteemed position as Chief of Forest Surveys in Washington D.C.
